topics.name: Circumference and area of a circle
topics.scopeNote: Added topic. Whole-circle and semicircle recap that boards still test (2024 main, 2025 compartment, 2026 second).

patterns.pattern: Ratio of radii or areas from the ratio of circumferences
patterns.sample: The circumferences of two circles are in the ratio $3:5$. Find the ratio of their areas.

patterns.pattern: Find radius when a circle's area numerically equals a semicircle's perimeter

patterns.pattern: Ratio of areas of a circle and a square of equal perimeter

patterns.pattern: Assertion-reason: radius from circumference using $C = 2\pi r$
patterns.sample: Assertion: a circle of circumference $44\text{ cm}$ has radius $7\text{ cm}$ (use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$). Reason: $C = 2\pi r$.

patterns.pattern: Diameter or radius of a circle whose area equals the sum of the areas of two given circles
patterns.sample: Two circles have radii $5$ cm and $12$ cm. Find the radius of a circle whose area equals the sum of their areas. (Answer: $13$ cm)

patterns.pattern: Find the radius from a given circumference or a circumference-radius relation, then the circumference or area
patterns.sample: The circumference of a circle exceeds its radius by $37$ cm. Taking $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$, find its circumference. (Answer: $44$ cm)

patterns.pattern: Wire bounding one shape (e.g. an equilateral triangle of given area) is reshaped into a circle: find its radius or area
patterns.sample: A wire encloses an equilateral triangle of area $121\sqrt{3}$ cm$^2$. It is bent into a circle. Taking $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$, find the area of the circle. (Answer: $346.5$ cm$^2$)

patterns.pattern: Area or side of the square inscribed in a circle of given radius (diagonal equals diameter)
patterns.sample: A square is inscribed in a circle of radius $5\sqrt{2}$ cm. Find the area of the square. (Answer: $100$ cm$^2$)

patterns.pattern: Assertion-reason: scaling the radius of a sector
patterns.sample: Assertion: if the radius of a sector is tripled at the same angle, its area becomes $9$ times. Reason: area of a sector is $\frac{\theta}{360}\pi r^2$.

patterns.pattern: Assertion-reason: what the perimeter of a sector includes
patterns.sample: Assertion: a sector of radius $14\text{ cm}$ and angle $90^\circ$ has perimeter $50\text{ cm}$ (use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$). Reason: perimeter of a sector equals arc length plus $2r$.

patterns.pattern: Sector area from radius and sector perimeter
patterns.sample: A sector of radius $7\text{ cm}$ has perimeter $25\text{ cm}$. Find the area of the sector.

patterns.pattern: Radius and area from sector perimeter and central angle
patterns.sample: A sector of central angle $90^\circ$ has perimeter $50\text{ cm}$. Find its radius and area. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Perimeter of a sector-shaped object in a real setting
patterns.sample: A table top is a sector of radius $1.4\text{ m}$ and central angle $90^\circ$. Find the length of edging needed around it. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Radius from sector area and arc length
patterns.sample: A sector has area $154\text{ cm}^2$ and arc length $22\text{ cm}$. Find the radius of the circle and the central angle. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Sector area and arc length from radius and angle
patterns.sample: For a circle of radius $21\text{ cm}$ and a central angle of $120^\circ$, find the area of the sector and the length of the arc. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Areas of minor and major sectors
patterns.sample: A circle has radius $14\text{ cm}$. An arc subtends $60^\circ$ at the centre. Find the areas of the minor and major sectors. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Area and perimeter of one of n equal sectors from the diameter
patterns.sample: A circle of diameter $28\text{ cm}$ is divided into $8$ equal sectors. Find the area and the perimeter of one sector. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Angle, arc and perimeter from sector area and radius
patterns.sample: A sector of radius $14\text{ cm}$ has area $77\text{ cm}^2$. Find (i) its central angle, (ii) its arc length, (iii) its perimeter. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Compare the area and perimeter of two different sectors
patterns.sample: Sector $X$ has radius $21\text{ cm}$ and angle $120^\circ$; sector $Y$ has radius $28\text{ cm}$ and angle $90^\circ$. Find the differences in their areas and perimeters. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Combined area of three shaded sectors with marked angles (figure)
patterns.sample: In a circle of radius $14\text{ cm}$, three shaded sectors have angles $40^\circ$, $80^\circ$ and $60^\circ$. Find the total shaded area. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Bent wire forms a sector boundary: arc, angle, area and fraction of the circle
patterns.sample: A wire $64\text{ cm}$ long forms the boundary of a sector of radius $21\text{ cm}$. Find the arc length, the central angle, the area and the fraction of the circle's area. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Radius and angle from sector perimeter and area, via a quadratic (cross-chapter)
patterns.sample: A sector has perimeter $25\text{ cm}$ and area $38.5\text{ cm}^2$, with a whole-number radius. Form a quadratic in $r$, then find $r$, the arc length and the central angle. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Case study: circle divided by diameters into equal sectors (brooch, pizza)
patterns.sample: A brooch of diameter $28\text{ mm}$ is divided into $10$ equal sectors by $5$ diameters. (i) Find each sector's angle. (ii) Find one arc's length. (iii) Find one sector's area. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Assertion-reason: arc length is proportional to the central angle
patterns.sample: Assertion: arcs of one circle subtending $30^\circ$ and $90^\circ$ have lengths in the ratio $1:3$. Reason: arc length is directly proportional to the central angle.

patterns.pattern: Arc with radius or angle missing: find it, then the sector area
patterns.sample: An arc of length $44\text{ cm}$ lies on a circle of radius $42\text{ cm}$. Find the central angle and the area of the sector. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Equal arcs in two circles: common length and unknown radius
patterns.sample: An arc of a circle of radius $21\text{ cm}$ subtends $120^\circ$. An equal arc of a second circle subtends $90^\circ$. Find the arc length and the second radius. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

topics.name: Segment area
topics.scopeNote: Central angles kept to 60, 90 and 120 degrees.

patterns.pattern: Choose the segment-area expression in terms of $r$ for a standard angle
patterns.sample: The area of the minor segment of a circle of radius $r$ for a central angle of $60^\circ$ is:

patterns.pattern: Numerical minor segment area at 60 or 90 degrees
patterns.sample: A chord of a circle of radius $14\text{ cm}$ subtends a right angle at the centre. The area of the minor segment is (use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$):

patterns.pattern: Radius from a given minor segment area
patterns.sample: The minor segment cut by a chord subtending $90^\circ$ at the centre has area $56\text{ cm}^2$. The radius of the circle is (use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$):

patterns.pattern: Major segment as circle minus a given minor segment

patterns.pattern: Minor segment area in two marks
patterns.sample: A chord of a circle of radius $14\text{ cm}$ subtends $90^\circ$ at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Major segment area in two marks
patterns.sample: A chord of a circle of radius $10\text{ cm}$ subtends a right angle at the centre. Find the area of the major segment. (Use $\pi = 3.14$)

patterns.pattern: Minor segment area from radius and central angle
patterns.sample: A chord of a circle of radius $21\text{ cm}$ subtends $60^\circ$ at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$, $\sqrt{3} = 1.73$)

patterns.pattern: Minor segment area when the chord length is given, radius not
patterns.sample: A chord of length $10\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$ subtends a right angle at the centre. Find the radius and the area of the minor segment. (Use $\pi = 3.14$)

patterns.pattern: Perimeter of a shaded segment: arc plus chord (figure)
patterns.sample: Chord $AB$ of a circle of radius $21\text{ cm}$ subtends $120^\circ$ at the centre. Find the perimeter of the shaded minor segment. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Major sector perimeter and segment area, with triangle area supplied (figure)
patterns.sample: Chord $AB$ subtends $90^\circ$ at the centre $O$ of a circle of radius $14\text{ cm}$, and $\triangle OAB$ has area $98\text{ cm}^2$. Find the major sector's perimeter and the minor segment's area. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Minor and major segment areas, with chord or triangle as sub-parts
patterns.sample: A chord of a circle of radius $14\text{ cm}$ subtends $120^\circ$ at the centre. Find the areas of the triangle, the minor segment and the major segment. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$, $\sqrt{3} = 1.73$)

patterns.pattern: Arc length and minor segment area for one chord
patterns.sample: A chord of a circle of radius $21\text{ cm}$ subtends $60^\circ$ at the centre. Find the length of the arc and the area of the minor segment. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$, $\sqrt{3} = 1.73$)

patterns.pattern: Case study: a straight fence or path cuts a segment from a circular field
patterns.sample: A straight path $AB$ crosses a circular park of radius $21\text{ m}$, subtending $90^\circ$ at the centre. (i) Find $AB$. (ii) Find the area of $\triangle OAB$. (iii) Find the minor segment's area. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

topics.name: Combination figures (shaded regions)
topics.scopeNote: The combination-of-plane-figures section is believed cut, but recent papers still test it: 2024 main has horses at the four corners of a square, 2025 main has a square house inside a circular plot, and 2025 compartment and 2026 second both have shaded-area diagrams. So B, E and MCQ patterns carry real targets. C and D patterns have target 0: their board evidence is 2016-2019 only, and core patterns fill those slots. A person must confirm the syllabus; if the section is out, remove this topic and rebalance.

patterns.pattern: Assertion-reason: area of a ring
patterns.sample: Assertion: the ring between concentric circles of radii $5\text{ cm}$ and $3\text{ cm}$ has area $16\pi\text{ cm}^2$. Reason: the area of a ring is $\pi(R^2 - r^2)$.

patterns.pattern: Rectangle minus a circle lying inside it
patterns.sample: A rectangular lawn $40\text{ m}$ by $25\text{ m}$ contains a circular pond of radius $7\text{ m}$. Find the area of the lawn outside the pond. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Rectangle plus a semicircle (window), with cost
patterns.sample: A window is a rectangle $1.4\text{ m}$ wide and $1.5\text{ m}$ high with a semicircle on top of its width. Find the glass area and its cost at ₹$400$ per $\text{m}^2$. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Total shaded area of three marked sectors, answer in $\pi$ (figure)
patterns.sample: Three shaded sectors of a circle of radius $6\text{ cm}$ have angles $40^\circ$, $50^\circ$ and $30^\circ$. Find the total shaded area in terms of $\pi$.

patterns.pattern: Gap between three touching circles in two marks (figure)
patterns.sample: Three equal circles of radius $14\text{ cm}$ touch one another. Find the area of the shaded region between them. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Shaded area read from a diagram: polygon minus a marked sector (figure)
patterns.sample: Trapezium $ABCD$ has $AB \parallel CD$, $AB = 10\text{ cm}$, $CD = 6\text{ cm}$, $AD = 7\text{ cm}$ and $\angle A = 90^\circ$. A quadrant of radius $3.5\text{ cm}$ centred at $A$ is removed. Find the remaining area. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Semicircle minus the right triangle inscribed in it (figure)
patterns.sample: $AB = 13\text{ cm}$ is the diameter of a semicircle and $C$ lies on the arc with $AC = 5\text{ cm}$. Find the area of the semicircle outside $\triangle ABC$. (Use $\pi = 3.14$)

patterns.pattern: Region between concentric circles for a marked central angle (figure)
patterns.sample: Concentric circles have radii $7\text{ cm}$ and $14\text{ cm}$. Find the area of the part of the ring lying within a central angle of $60^\circ$. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Square minus four corner quadrants
patterns.sample: A square of side $14\text{ cm}$ has quadrants of radius $7\text{ cm}$ centred at each corner. Find the area of the square outside them. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Circle or quadrant minus an inscribed rectangle or square (figure)
patterns.sample: A rectangle $8\text{ cm}$ by $6\text{ cm}$ is inscribed in a circle. Find the area of the circle outside the rectangle. (Use $\pi = 3.14$)

patterns.pattern: Circular path inside a rectangular park, with turfing cost
patterns.sample: A park $40\text{ m}$ by $25\text{ m}$ has a central fountain of radius $7\text{ m}$ ringed by a path $3.5\text{ m}$ wide. Find the area of the path and of the remaining park. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Rectangle with semicircles cut in on two sides: area and perimeter
patterns.sample: From a plate $40\text{ cm}$ by $14\text{ cm}$, a semicircle is cut inward on each $14\text{ cm}$ side. Find the area and perimeter of the remaining plate. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Prove that crescents on an inscribed square equal the square in area
patterns.sample: A square is inscribed in a circle of radius $7\text{ cm}$, with outward semicircles on its sides. Show that the four crescents between the semicircles and the circle have total area equal to the square.

patterns.pattern: Sector with a tangent at a radius's end: boundary or area of the outer region, using trigonometry (figure)
patterns.sample: Sector $OAP$ has radius $7\text{ cm}$ and angle $60^\circ$. The tangent at $A$ meets $OP$ produced at $B$. Find the perimeter of the region bounded by $AB$, $BP$ and arc $AP$. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Rectangle with outward semicircles (running track): perimeter and area
patterns.sample: A track is a rectangle $40\text{ m}$ by $14\text{ m}$ with outward semicircles on the $14\text{ m}$ sides. Find the perimeter and the area of the figure. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Square tile with inscribed circle and inner circle: combined design area
patterns.sample: A tile of side $14\text{ cm}$ has an inscribed circle and a concentric circle of radius $3.5\text{ cm}$. Find the total area of the four corners and the ring. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Case study: rectangle with quadrants or semicircles attached (memento, playground)
patterns.sample: A board $28\text{ cm}$ by $14\text{ cm}$ has quadrants of radius $14\text{ cm}$ centred at the two ends of a long side. (i) Find one quadrant's area. (ii) Find one arc's length. (iii) Find the remaining area. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Case study: animals tied at the corners of a square field
patterns.sample: Horses are tied at the four corners of a square field of side $28\text{ m}$ with $7\text{ m}$ ropes. (i) Find the field's area. (ii) Find the grazed area. (iii) Find the ungrazed area if ropes become $14\text{ m}$. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Case study: polygon inside a circle or semicircle (house on a plot, farm on a semicircle)
patterns.sample: A largest square house stands inside a circular plot of radius $14\text{ m}$. (i) Find the fence length around the plot. (ii) Find the house's side. (iii) Find the area left for grass. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Case study: rings of rope with an equilateral triangle marking a shaded segment
patterns.sample: A ring is made from $44\text{ m}$ of rope, with equilateral $\triangle OAB$ drawn from its centre $O$. (i) Find the radius. (ii) State $\angle AOB$. (iii) Find the area of the segment on $AB$. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

patterns.pattern: Shaded area of a composite figure built from a polygon with circles, semicircles or arcs (add and subtract pieces) (figure)
patterns.sample: $ABCD$ is a square of side $14$ cm. Semicircles are drawn inward on each side as diameter. Find the area of the shaded region where the semicircles overlap. (Answer: $112$ cm$^2$)

patterns.sample: A car has two non-overlapping wipers, each with a blade of $21\text{ cm}$ sweeping $120^\circ$. Find the total area cleaned in one sweep. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
